biography: Malo Bolliet, a name synonymous with frustrating inconsistency in French karting circles, hails from the small village of Saint-Pourçain-sur-Sioule. His racing journey began, as it often does, with a childhood fascination for anything with wheels. At the tender age of 10, he received a hand-me-down kart from his uncle, a former regional champion. This sparked an obsession that consumed his youth. Early promise quickly faded into a pattern of flashes of brilliance marred by unforced errors. One defining moment came at the 2008 French National Karting Championship where, starting from pole position in the final race, he spun out on the first lap, gifting the victory to his arch-rival. Now at 38, Bolliet is considered a veteran, still competing at a regional level, clinging to the dream of recapturing his early potential, even though the reality paints a different picture. He continues to participate, a testament to his enduring love for karting, even if success remains elusive.
drivingStyle: Bolliet's driving style can be described as aggressive and occasionally reckless. He is known for late-braking maneuvers and a willingness to take risks in corners, often pushing his kart to its absolute limit. Tire management is not his forte; he tends to overdrive early in a race, leading to significant degradation in the later stages. Under pressure, his inconsistency becomes even more pronounced, as he is prone to making costly mistakes when the stakes are high.

rivalries.reason: Dubois and Bolliet have a long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial collision in the 2008 French National Karting Championship where Dubois accused Bolliet of deliberately taking him out.
Leclerc consistently outperformed Bolliet, a fact he found particularly galling, fueling a personal rivalry based on professional jealousy.
Moreau, a young prodigy, openly dismissed Bolliet as 'past his prime,' which Bolliet took as a personal affront and a challenge to prove him wrong.

quirks: Always wears the same faded blue racing gloves, claiming they bring him luck, despite overwhelming evidence to the contrary.
Refuses to start a race without listening to a specific Serge Gainsbourg song, 'Bonnie and Clyde,' regardless of the track or conditions.
Has a pre-race ritual of meticulously cleaning his visor three times, even if it's already spotless.
famousQuote: "Sometimes, the only difference between genius and madness is the result."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2007 Coupe de France régionale karting championship after a daring last-lap overtake, a victory he still considers his greatest achievement.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out on the final corner of the 2012 French National Karting Championship while leading, costing him a potential national title.
